rule.1 clock: every page counts at the clock its own cells measured, never the lock asked, and no absolute reading of a field with a known bias enters a verdict. sm_clock_mhz (cycles over ncu's duration) reads about 1.4% low uniformly, so it may enter only as a ratio of two captures, where the bias cancels. Per scorer: part 3 (score_const) K1, K2 and K4 are in SM cycles and read no clock; K3's rho_f = f_1005 / f_1710 is a ratio of the two captures' median per-cell sm_clock_mhz, so the bias cancels; each capture's clock_mhz is printed only; the identification reads only K1 to K4. Part 4 (score_w1floor) is in SM cycles (slopes over grid x S / 132, the registered asymptote in cycles per k-step) and reads no clock. Part 1 (score_knobs) reads DRAM and L2 bytes and occupancy, clock-free. Part 2 (score_launch) compares host-timed milliseconds with the registered C_reg and F; no verdict reads a clock field (cells.csv's NVML sm_clock_load_mhz is not read), and repricing C_reg would change a registered prediction, which this addendum does not do. No scorer used a nominal lock clock or an absolute measured clock in a verdict, and none is changed on this account
rule.2 above-lock cells: a (cell, GEMM) of a floor capture taken under a lock whose own sm_clock_mhz is above that capture's lock by more than one step (15 MHz) is dropped, in both views, and recorded. A clock above the lock cannot be run; such readings come only from short GEMMs, where ncu's fixed duration offset dominates the cycles-over-duration ratio. Base-clock captures carry no lock and drop nothing; byte pages are not touched (their scores read no clock, and the knobs registration states V10 gates no score). The comparison reads sm_clock_mhz absolutely against the lock; its known bias is downward (about -1.4%, some 24 MHz at 1710), so it can only leave an above-lock cell in, never drop a cell that ran at the lock. It decides which cells are kept, not any verdict's value
rule.3 two views: every verdict (each K and the identification of part 3; the part-4 families, theta call, w2 offset and co-primary per-cell test; every part-1 test, control-dependent verdict, partition cross-check and T5 candidate; every part-2 P) is computed twice: ALL, every page counted under rules 1 and 2, gate-failed pages included; CLEAN, every page that failed a validity gate excluded (for a floor capture under a lock, the lock check of rule 5 in place of FL1). The registered verdict is the common one when ALL and CLEAN agree; INCONCLUSIVE when they disagree; NOT SCORED when CLEAN has no data and ALL does, with ALL's verdict printed beside, labelled as reading only gate-failed pages (the label means that verdict exists only because gate-failed pages were read; K3, for one, reads the 1005 capture beside a 1710 one)
rule.4 other gates: a page that fails any validity gate other than FL1 is handled by the same rule. A gate fails when its verdict is anything but PASS (FAIL or REFUSE); CLAIM gates (C1 to C6) are findings, not validity gates, and gate nothing
rule.V1: a page whose V1 (launch attribution) failed is unusable in both views: a launch counted into the wrong slot moves every number after it
rule.registered handling kept: where a registration already states a gate's handling, that statement stands and the gate is not a CLEAN exclusion there: in part 1 a V6 failure flags the page and its verdicts read INCONCLUSIVE in both views, and V10 gates no part-1 score (bytes are clock-free)
rule.5 CLEAN for floor captures: for a floor capture taken under a lock, CLEAN does not use FL1. It uses V1 PASS (rule V1) and a lock-in-force check from an independent clock: the median over the capture's cells of the null kernel's sm_clock_mhz within 3% of the lock. Its bias is a uniform -1.4%; 3% passes a held lock and catches one not in force (the 2026-09-28 8x22B floor, about +5.6%). Where a capture has no null kernel, CLEAN falls back to FL1. FL1 is still recorded and printed per page and still decides nothing else. Base-clock captures carry no lock and no check. This check was chosen after the rental-2 pages' gate outcomes and null-kernel clock medians were seen (tp8, tp4, tp2 1710 medians 1684, 1687, 1688 MHz; tp4 1005 median 991 MHz) and before any score was computed. FL1 is set aside for this because of the gate audit of the published pre-rental-2 data (scratchpad gate-audit/AUDIT.md): whenever its fitted t0 is small its fitted f reads low (a degenerate f / t0 fit), while cell-matched lock / base ratios and the L2 counter's clock show the locks held; the only real off-lock floor (8x22B, the lock not in force) was a gross error
